info.title: Lunedo API
info.description:
The Lunedo API lets scripts and integrations read and change the data of this instance. Every route is versioned under `/api/v1`.

## Create a token

Scripts authenticate with an API token. There are two kinds:

- **Personal tokens** act as your own account. Create one while signed in, in your account settings under Security.
- **Service account tokens** act as a service account of an organization, which keeps working when people leave. Holders of the "integrations and API" area create service accounts and their tokens.

A token starts with `ld_` and is shown only once, when it is created. Choose its scopes from the permission areas, each with `view` or `manage`, and optionally limit it to one organization. At every request, the token can do only what both its scopes and its owner's current permissions allow. A token has no expiry unless you set a date when you create it. If the instance or an organization sets a maximum lifetime, every new token needs a date within it, and a token created without one gets the maximum. Creating and revoking tokens needs a signed-in session; a token cannot manage tokens.

## Your first request

Send the token in the `Authorization` header. Tokens in the query string are never accepted, and a request that carries both a session cookie and a token is rejected.

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ld_..." https://wiki.example.org/api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}
```

Requests with a token need no cross-site request header.

## Pagination

Lists return one page at a time:

```json
{ "items": [], "nextCursor": "eyJ..." }
```

Pass `nextCursor` as the `cursor` query parameter to get the next page, until `nextCursor` is `null`. `limit` sets the page size, from 1 to 200, default 50.

## Errors

Errors follow RFC 9457 Problem Details with the media type `application/problem+json`. Branch on `type`; it is stable, for example `urn:lunedo:problem:forbidden`. `code` repeats its last part. Invalid input lists the affected fields in `fields`.

## Rate limits

Each token may send a configurable number of requests per minute, 600 by default. Above that, the API answers `429` with the problem type `urn:lunedo:problem:rateLimited` and a `Retry-After` header with the seconds to wait.

Needs a signed-in session.

anyOf.description: Who may read a knowledge base: `public` (everyone, also without signing in, once the portal exists; in Lunedo all internal users), `signedIn` (all internal users of the instance), `groups` (members of the groups that hold the reader role) or `portal` (portal accounts; in Lunedo only holders of a role). source.description: What is imported: `confluence-xml` for the XML space export of Confluence Cloud or Data Center, `confluence-csv` for the CSV space export of Confluence Cloud, `confluence-cloud` and `confluence-dc` to read a space through the Confluence API, `markdown` for a ZIP file of Markdown files, `word` for Word documents (`.docx`). state.description: State of the import. `draft` while the wizard is filled in, `analyzing` while the export is read, `ready` when it can be started, `running` while it imports, `held` when the importing administrator lost the permission and another administrator has to take over, `stopping` and `discarding` while the quarantine space is deleted, `review` when the quarantine space waits for a decision, `accepted`, `discarded`, `stopped` and `failed` at the end. A re-import is in `running` while it compares or applies, in `review` while changes wait for a decision, `accepted` when everything is applied, and `superseded` when a newer re-import of the same space replaced it. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

draftStep.description: Step of the wizard the importer was on, for continuing a draft.

kind.description: Where the export comes from. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

size.description: Size in bytes, or null when not known yet.

uploadId.description: ID of the upload, or null for a file in the import folder.

complete.description: Whether the file is complete and can be read.

file.description: The export file, or null when none is chosen yet.

put.summary: Connect an import to Confluence
put.description:
Sets how an import of the source `confluence-cloud` or `confluence-dc` reads Confluence through its API. Lunedo tests the connection at once, stores the token encrypted, uses it only for this import and the imports of further spaces chosen with it, and deletes it when the last of them is accepted, discarded, stopped or fails, when the importer loses the permission to import, or when the draft is left alone for a week. Only `https` sites under `atlassian.net` or hosts the instance administrator allowed are contacted, never addresses in private networks unless the instance allows them, and redirects are not followed.

Requires the permission `import.manage` on the import in `importId`.

baseUrl.description: Address Confluence is opened with, including a context path, such as `https://wiki.example.com/confluence`.

token.description: Personal access token. It is stored encrypted.

schema.description: How Lunedo reads Confluence through its API.

organizationId.description: Organization the import belongs to.

source.description: What is imported: `confluence-xml` for the XML space export of Confluence Cloud or Data Center, `confluence-csv` for the CSV space export of Confluence Cloud, `confluence-cloud` and `confluence-dc` to read a space through the Confluence API, `markdown` for a ZIP file of Markdown files, `word` for Word documents (`.docx`). New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

state.description: State of the import. `draft` while the wizard is filled in, `analyzing` while the export is read, `ready` when it can be started, `running` while it imports, `held` when the importing administrator lost the permission and another administrator has to take over, `stopping` and `discarding` while the quarantine space is deleted, `review` when the quarantine space waits for a decision, `accepted`, `discarded`, `stopped` and `failed` at the end. A re-import is in `running` while it compares or applies, in `review` while changes wait for a decision, `accepted` when everything is applied, and `superseded` when a newer re-import of the same space replaced it. put.summary: Choose the Confluence spaces to import
put.description:
Chooses one or more spaces of the connection of an import draft. Each space is imported on its own, into its own new space, with its own check, dry run, report and re-import. The import keeps its space when it is chosen; Lunedo creates a draft for every other space that shares the connection and its token, and removes the drafts of spaces no longer chosen. Imports sharing a connection read and run one after another. The shared token is deleted when the last of them has ended or been removed. A re-import reads only the space it came from.

Requires the permission `import.manage` on the import in `importId`.

spaceKeys.description: Keys of the Confluence spaces to import, 1 to 50. The import keeps its space when it is in the list; every other space gets an import of its own over the same connection, and drafts of spaces no longer listed are removed.

organizationId.description: Organization the import belongs to.

source.description: What is imported: `confluence-xml` for the XML space export of Confluence Cloud or Data Center, `confluence-csv` for the CSV space export of Confluence Cloud, `confluence-cloud` and `confluence-dc` to read a space through the Confluence API, `markdown` for a ZIP file of Markdown files, `word` for Word documents (`.docx`). New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

state.description: State of the import. `draft` while the wizard is filled in, `analyzing` while the export is read, `ready` when it can be started, `running` while it imports, `held` when the importing administrator lost the permission and another administrator has to take over, `stopping` and `discarding` while the quarantine space is deleted, `review` when the quarantine space waits for a decision, `accepted`, `discarded`, `stopped` and `failed` at the end. A re-import is in `running` while it compares or applies, in `review` while changes wait for a decision, `accepted` when everything is applied, and `superseded` when a newer re-import of the same space replaced it. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

put.summary: Set the reviewers of an import
put.description:
Replaces the reviewers. Reviewers can read the quarantine space and the report, but cannot accept, discard or stop the import. The change is audited.

Requires the permission `import.manage` on the import in `importId`.

items.description: ID of a member of the organization.

New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

state.description: State of the import. `draft` while the wizard is filled in, `analyzing` while the export is read, `ready` when it can be started, `running` while it imports, `held` when the importing administrator lost the permission and another administrator has to take over, `stopping` and `discarding` while the quarantine space is deleted, `review` when the quarantine space waits for a decision, `accepted`, `discarded`, `stopped` and `failed` at the end. A re-import is in `running` while it compares or applies, in `review` while changes wait for a decision, `accepted` when everything is applied, and `superseded` when a newer re-import of the same space replaced it. state.description: State of the import. `draft` while the wizard is filled in, `analyzing` while the export is read, `ready` when it can be started, `running` while it imports, `held` when the importing administrator lost the permission and another administrator has to take over, `stopping` and `discarding` while the quarantine space is deleted, `review` when the quarantine space waits for a decision, `accepted`, `discarded`, `stopped` and `failed` at the end. A re-import is in `running` while it compares or applies, in `review` while changes wait for a decision, `accepted` when everything is applied, and `superseded` when a newer re-import of the same space replaced it. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

Nobody can sign in through the provider any more, synchronization stops and the sessions that came from it end. Everything else stays and returns when the provider is activated again.

Requires the permission `instance.signIn.manage` on the instance. Needs a signed-in session; API tokens are refused.

put.summary: Switch maintenance mode
put.description:
Switches maintenance mode on or off, or changes its message and whether signing in is paused. While it is on, the instance is read-only for everyone, also for instance administrators: changes through the API are refused, open editors switch to read-only, and background jobs that change content wait. Backups, safety-net sweeps, mail delivery, SCIM and identity provider synchronization keep running. With `blockSignIn`, only instance administrators can sign in; existing sessions of others are not ended. Every switch and change is recorded in the audit log.

Requires the permission `instance.operations.manage` on the instance.

post.description:
Copies a page, a folder or a whiteboard, optionally with everything below it, within its space or into another space of the same organization. Each copy starts from the published version with one version in its history, gets the current version of every attachment, the labels, page properties, options and status, and belongs to the caller. Comments, reactions, watchers, shares and links stay behind. Links between copied pages point to the copies. When people could read the copy who cannot read the source, the copy is refused with `copyChangesAccess` unless the request carries the confirmation of a preview of exactly that change. Copies of up to 20 items finish within the request; larger ones answer with state `queued`, run in the background and notify the caller at the end; a failed copy leaves nothing behind.

Requires the permission `item.view` on the item in `itemId`.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: ID of the page, folder or whiteboard.

spaceId.description: Target space. Leave it out to copy within the space.

parentId.description: Parent item at the target, or null for the root of the tree.

beforeId.description: Place the copy directly before this sibling.

afterId.description: Place the copy directly after this sibling.

descendants.description: Copy the items below as well. Default false: only the item itself.

Returns the same item as `GET /items/{itemId}`, found by the number in its address in the app. A number that does not exist and a number of an item the caller cannot see give the same `notFound` answer.

Requires the permission `item.view` on the item in `number`.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Number of the item, as shown in the addresses of the app.

number.description: Number of the item in the addresses of the app, unique in the instance. It never changes and is never reused.

parentId.description: Parent item, or null at the root of the tree.

kind.description: `page`, `folder`, `link`, `blogPost`, `meetingSeries`, `meetingTopic` or `whiteboard`. Blog posts and topics are not part of the tree; they appear in the blog and the meetings of their space. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

title.description: Title. Empty for a link to content the caller cannot read.

numberHeadings.description: Whether the headings of the page are numbered in the page, in print and in Word.

mode.description: Editing mode of a page: `publish` (readers see the last published version while editors work on a draft) or `live` (readers see every change at once). Folders and links are always `live`.

published.description: Whether readers can see the page. False for a page in publish mode that was never published; only editors see it.

archived.description: Whether the item is archived. Archived items are read-only.

position.description: Sort key among the siblings. Items sort by it in binary order.

viewRestriction.description: Whether only an access list may view the item: set on the item itself, on a page above, or not at all.

editRestricted.description: Whether only an access list may edit the item.

itemId.description: Linked page, folder or whiteboard, or null for an address or when the caller cannot read it.

url.description: Linked `http` or `https` address, or null.

accessible.description: Whether the caller can open the target. If not, the title is empty.

inTrash.description: Whether the target is in the trash. Only true for callers who could read it before.

number.description: Number of the target in the addresses of the app.

kind.description: Kind of the target. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

target.description: The linked page, folder or whiteboard, or null.

anyOf.description: Where a link in the page tree points.

link.description: Target of a link, or null for pages and folders.

creatorId.description: Account that created the item, or null.

anyOf.description: Content language as an ISO 639-1 code, or `other` for a language without its own word matching. Words are then matched as written. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

contentLanguage.description: Language of the page content for search, or null to use the language of the space.

anyOf.description: Type of an article: `howTo` (step-by-step instructions) or `troubleshooting` (symptom, cause and solution). New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

articleType.description: Type of an article in a knowledge base, or null for other items and articles without a type.

translationOf.description: Original article of a translation in a knowledge base, or null. A translation is listed below its original; `contentLanguage` is its language.

ownerId.description: Owner of the item, or null. The owner stays set when the person leaves; `owner.active` in the item details says whether the item has an active owner.

builtIn.description: Which default value this is, or null for a value a space admin added. Clients show the translated name of a default value unless `name` is set. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

name.description: Name set by a space admin, or null to show the default name.

anyOf.description: A page status.

status.description: Status of a page, or null when it has none or page status is turned off in the space.

createdAt.description: When the item was created. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the item last changed in the tree. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

contentUpdatedAt.description: When the content of the page last changed. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

spaceKey.description: Key of the space. Empty when the caller sees the item only through a share or link.

spaceName.description: Name of the space. Empty when the caller sees the item only through a share or link.

spaceAccess.description: Whether the caller has access to the space; false when the item is visible only through a share or link.

spaceContentLanguage.description: Content language of the space, which pages without a content language of their own use for search.

number.description: Number of the ancestor in the addresses of the app.

kind.description: Kind of the ancestor. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

published.description: Whether the ancestor counts as published: a folder, a link, a page in live mode or a page with a published version. Readers see a page only when every ancestor is published.

ancestors.description: Ancestors from the root down to the parent.

name.description: Name of the owner, or null when the caller may not see the person.

jobTitle.description: Job title the person entered on their profile, or null.

pictureRef.description: Version of the profile picture, or null without one. Changes whenever the picture changes; load the picture from `GET /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/picture`.

email.description: E-mail address of the owner, or null when the caller may not see it.

active.description: Whether the owner can still act: false when the account is deactivated or its membership in the organization ended.

owner.description: Owner of the item, or null when it has none.

ownershipTransferable.description: Whether the caller may give the item a new owner.

schema.description: An item with its place in the tree.

get.summary: Get the maintenance mode
get.description: Tells whether the instance is in maintenance mode, with the message of the instance administrators. While it is on, every change through the API is refused with `503` and the problem `maintenanceMode`; reading, search and exports of single pages keep working. Anyone can read this, also without signing in, so that the sign-in page can show the banner.

enabled.description: Whether the instance is in maintenance mode and refuses changes.

message.description: The message of the instance administrators shown in the banner. Empty when they wrote none.

blockSignIn.description: Whether signing in is paused for everyone except instance administrators.

startedAt.description: When maintenance mode was switched on, or null when it is off.

schema.description: The maintenance mode of the instance.

example.message: Update to 1.5 until 18:00. Pages can be read, but not changed.

put.summary: End a meeting series or continue it
put.description:
Ending archives the series with its meetings and topics: read-only and without a next meeting. Continuing brings it back; when its former parent page is in the trash and the series would lose a view restriction it inherited, continuing is refused with `restrictedParentInTrash` until that page is restored.

Requires the permission `item.archive` on the item in `seriesId`.

get.summary: Get a meeting
get.description:
Returns state, time and attendees of a meeting. The notes are the content of the meeting page; read them through the page content.

Requires the permission `item.view` on the item in `meetingId`.

number.description: Number of the meeting page in the addresses of the app.

seriesId.description: The series, or null when the caller cannot read it.

seriesNumber.description: Number of the series in the addresses of the app, or null when the caller cannot read it.

seriesTitle.description: Name of the series, or null when the caller cannot read it.

state.description: `upcoming` is the next meeting, `closed` and `skipped` are done, `reopened` was closed and is open again. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

next.description: True for the next meeting of the series: the earliest one that is neither held nor skipped.

current.description: Whether the meeting is open: upcoming or reopened.

startsAt.description: Start, or null when not scheduled yet. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

recurrenceId.description: Original start in the rhythm, or null. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

timeZone.description: Time zone of the series, or null when the caller cannot read the series.

closedAt.description: When the meeting was closed or skipped. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

nextMeetingId.description: The meeting created when this one was closed or skipped, or null when the caller cannot read the series.

number.description: Number of the meeting in the addresses of the app.

startsAt.description: Start. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

anyOf.description: A neighboring meeting.

previousMeeting.description: The meeting of the series before this one that the caller can read, skipped ones left out.

number.description: Number of the meeting in the addresses of the app.

startsAt.description: Start. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

anyOf.description: A neighboring meeting.

followingMeeting.description: The meeting of the series after this one that the caller can read, skipped ones left out.

rhythm.description: Whether the series has a fixed rhythm; without one, closing asks for the next date. Null when the caller cannot read the series.

pictureRef.description: Version of the profile picture, or null without one. Changes whenever the picture changes; load the picture from `GET /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/picture`.

attendance.description: Attendance, or null when not recorded. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

member.description: Whether the person is a member of the series, or null when the caller cannot read it.

active.description: Whether the person can still take part: false when the account is deactivated, not set up yet or no longer a member of the organization. Always true for people the caller may not see.

canRead.description: Whether the person can read the meeting page.

extra.description: True for an additional meeting outside the rhythm.

note.description: Optional note, such as the company.

attendance.description: Attendance, or null when not recorded. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

items.description: A person without an account. Guests have no access to anything.

guests.description: Guests without an account, in order.

calendarUid.description: Calendar UID of the meeting when it comes from a calendar.

get.summary: Get the agenda of a meeting
get.description:
Returns the topics of the meeting in the order of the series: all open topics while the meeting is open, the discussed topics once it is closed. Each topic has this meeting's update, its earlier updates and its tasks. Also returns the decisions and tasks written in this meeting.

Requires the permission `item.view` on the item in `meetingId`.

meetingNumber.description: Number of the meeting in the addresses of the app.

seriesNumber.description: Number of its series in the addresses of the app.

current.description: True while the meeting is open: then the list holds all open topics. A closed meeting lists the topics it discussed.

number.description: Number of the topic in the addresses of the app.

status.description: Whether the topic is open. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

outcome.description: How a closed topic ended. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

oneOff.description: True for a topic of this meeting only; it closes with the meeting.

createdAt.description: When the topic was raised. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

text.description: The update of this meeting as plain text, paragraphs on own lines.

formatted.description: True when the update has formatting; change it in the notes then.

update.description: This meeting's update, or null when the notes have no block for the topic.

meetingNumber.description: Number of that meeting in the addresses of the app.

startsAt.description: Start of that meeting. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

previous.description: The last earlier updates the caller can read, newest first.

meetingNumber.description: Number of that meeting in the addresses of the app.

startsAt.description: Start of that meeting. ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

history.description: All updates of meetings before this one that the caller can read, oldest first. The first is the start of the topic.

meetings.description: How many meetings of the series the topic has been on, this one included.

done.description: Whether the task is done.

meetingId.description: Meeting the task was written in.

tasks.description: Tasks written in the updates of this topic.

topics.description: Topics in the order of the series.

closedTopics.description: How many topics were closed in this meeting.

topicTitle.description: Title of that topic, if visible.

done.description: Whether the task is done.

meetingId.description: Meeting the task was written in.

post.description:
Closes the meeting and notifies the attendees that the notes are available. Closing the upcoming meeting creates the next one: the next occurrence of the rhythm after now, or, without a fixed rhythm, at `nextStartsAt`. When two people close at the same moment, one succeeds and the other gets `meetingClosed`. A meeting can be closed from its day on, in the time zone of the series; before that the answer is `meetingInFuture`.

Requires the permission `item.edit` on the item in `meetingId`.

200.description: Server-sent events. The event `notifications` carries the unread count (`unreadCount`, at most 100, with `unreadCapped` true when there are more) at the start and after every change. The event `settings` names a setting whose value for the caller may have changed, with its level and, for an organization, the organization ID; reload the setting. The event `syncRuns` names a run of a provider's sync log that started, changed or ended, sent only to callers who may view sign-in providers; reload the sync log. The event `changes` names the kind of object that changed in the instance or in an organization, as recorded in the audit log, sent only to callers who may view such objects there or the audit log of that level; reload lists that show such objects. The event `spaces` names a space whose settings, access, page tree or page content changed, or where someone opened or left a page in the editor, with the kind of change and the affected item, sent only to callers who can read the space; reload what shows it. The event `imports` names an import whose state or progress changed, with its organization, sent only to callers who can see the import; reload it. The event `announcements` says that the announcement of the instance or of one of the caller's organizations changed; reload the announcements. The event `maintenance` says that maintenance mode was switched on or off or its message changed; reload `GET /api/v1/maintenance`.

get.summary: Search the content of an organization
get.description:
Searches pages, blog posts, comments, attachments, running topics and decisions of all spaces of the organization the caller can read, for the search page and for search while typing. The text of PDF, Word and Excel attachments is searched, file names of all attachments. Results, counts and excerpts only ever include content the caller can read; pages shared with the caller show no space or path. Drafts, attachments added only in a draft and private meeting notes are never searched. Unknown filter values and values of things the caller cannot see give the same empty answer.

Requires the permission `organization.search` on the organization in `organizationId`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The search text. Words must all match. `"exact phrase"` matches the words in this order, `-word` excludes a word, `OR` between two words matches either. The operators `space:KEY`, `label:name`, `author:name`, `status:name` (default values also by their English name, such as `status:verified`) and `type:page|blog|comment|attachment|topic|decision` filter like the parameters; quote values with spaces.

Restores a trash entry of either stage or a deleted space. Items return to their old place or the top level of their space. Confidential spaces are not reachable here; only their own space admins restore their content. When the former parent page is in the trash and the content would lose a view restriction it inherited, the restore is refused with `restrictedParentInTrash`; repeat it with `withParents=true` to restore the parent pages with it. `withParents=true` also restores a former parent page that is in the trash without a restriction, so the content returns below it.

post.summary: Export a page with its subpages
post.description:
Starts an export of the page and every subpage you can read: by default a ZIP archive with the page tree as folders, each page as Markdown and HTML and the attachments next to their pages; with a format, one print-ready HTML file, PDF file or Word document of all pages. Only space administrators, and organization administrators with access to the space outside confidential spaces, can start it. It is refused when the file store would pass the usage level where large writes are blocked (90 % by default), and stops when the usage reaches the critical level (95 % by default) while it is written. The export runs in the background. When it is ready, you get a notification with the download; only you can open it. The download is deleted 24 hours after it was first downloaded completely, or after 7 days if it is never downloaded. You can run one export at a time and keep up to 5; a new export of the same space or page replaces the earlier one.

Requires the permission `item.exportPages` on the item in `pageId`.

Returns in one answer what the app needs to show a page found by the number in its address: the item as `GET /items/by-number/{number}` returns it, the content readers see as `GET /pages/{pageId}/content` returns it, the statuses of its tasks and the caller's own access. `content` and `tasks` are null for an item that is not a page, and `content` also when the page has nothing readers may see yet. post.description:
Starts an export of every page of the space you can read: by default a ZIP archive with the page tree as folders, each page as Markdown and HTML, the attachments next to their pages and an index.html that lists the tree, where links between exported pages become relative paths; with a format, one print-ready HTML file, PDF file or Word document of all pages and published blog posts. Only space administrators, and organization administrators with access to the space outside confidential spaces, can start it. It is refused when the file store would pass the usage level where large writes are blocked (90 % by default), and stops when the usage reaches the critical level (95 % by default) while it is written. The export runs in the background. When it is ready, you get a notification with the download; only you can open it. The download is deleted 24 hours after it was first downloaded completely, or after 7 days if it is never downloaded. You can run one export at a time and keep up to 5; a new export of the same space or page replaces the earlier one.

Requires the permission `space.export` on the space in `spaceId`.

schema.description: What to export and how. Without a body, the export is a ZIP with every page as Markdown and HTML.

format.description: `archive` (the default) for a ZIP with every page as Markdown and HTML, `html` or `markdown` for a ZIP with one of them, `print` for one print-ready HTML file of up to 300 pages, `pdf` for one PDF file, which needs the optional render container, `docx` for one Word document. `site` for a ZIP with a static website of a public knowledge base: every published article, the start, category, search and contact pages, a search index, images and redirects for old addresses, with relative links so it works under any address.

attachments.description: Adds the attachments: next to their pages in a ZIP, as an appendix that lists them in `print`, `pdf` and `docx`. `archive` always contains them.

comments.description: Adds the open comments after each page in `print`, `pdf` and `docx`.

contents.description: Adds a table of contents in `print`, `pdf` and `docx`.

siteUrl.description: For `site`: the address the website will be served from, such as `https://help.example.org/`. With it, the website gets `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt` and language links for search engines; without it, they are left out.

scope.description: What is exported: `space` for a whole space, `pages` for a page with its subpages.

format.description: What the file contains: `archive` a ZIP with every page as Markdown and HTML, `html` or `markdown` a ZIP with one of them, `print` one print-ready HTML file, `pdf` one PDF file, `docx` one Word document, `site` a ZIP with a static website of a public knowledge base.

attachments.description: Whether the attachments are included or listed.

contents.description: Whether a table of contents is included.

spaceId.description: The exported space, or null when it was deleted since.

rootItemId.description: The exported page for `pages`, or null.

name.description: Name of the space or title of the page when the export was started.

state.description: `queued` waits for a worker, `running` is being built, `ready` can be downloaded, `failed` stopped with an error.

done.description: Files written so far.

total.description: Files in the export, 0 until known.

New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

Sets the audience. With `groups`, the listed groups get the reader role and groups that are no longer listed lose it; groups with a higher role keep it. A change that lets more people read needs `confirmWidening`. Every change is audited.

Requires the permission `space.manage` on the space in `spaceId`.

audience.description: Who may read a knowledge base: `public` (everyone, also without signing in, once the portal exists; in Lunedo all internal users), `signedIn` (all internal users of the instance), `groups` (members of the groups that hold the reader role) or `portal` (portal accounts; in Lunedo only holders of a role). Categories and articles can narrow it with view restrictions, never widen it. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

groupIds.description: Groups that may read the knowledge base when `audience` is `groups`. Ignored otherwise.

confirmWidening.description: Confirms a change that lets more people read the knowledge base. Without it such a change is refused.

Categories and articles can narrow it with view restrictions, never widen it. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.

key.description: Key of the space, 2 to 10 letters or digits. It appears in addresses.

anyOf.description: Who may read a knowledge base: `public` (everyone, also without signing in, once the portal exists; in Lunedo all internal users), `signedIn` (all internal users of the instance), `groups` (members of the groups that hold the reader role) or `portal` (portal accounts; in Lunedo only holders of a role). Categories and articles can narrow it with view restrictions, never widen it. New values can be added in later versions; handle unknown values.
